One-liner: 34-year-old woman at 38 weeks gestation with severe headache and elevated blood pressures.

Chief complaint: Headache.

History of present illness: 34-year-old G2P1 at 38w2d who presents with severe frontal headache for 6 hours, described as the worst headache of her life, associated with visual spots and right upper quadrant pain. Blood pressure at home 168/104. Denies fever, contractions, fluid leakage, vaginal bleeding. Fetal movement normal. No seizure.

Past medical history: Gestational hypertension diagnosed at 36 weeks.

Medications: Prenatal vitamin daily; Labetalol 200 mg BID (started 2 days ago).

Social history: Married, works as a teacher. No tobacco, alcohol, or drugs.

Review of systems: Headache, visual changes, RUQ pain as above. Denies dyspnea, chest pain, edema changes.

Physical exam: BP 172/108 (repeat 170/106), HR 92, RR 18, SpO2 99% RA, Temp 98.2 F. Fundi: no papilledema. DTRs 3+ with clonus. Abdomen: gravid, tender RUQ. No peripheral edema noted. FHTs 140s, reassuring.

Laboratory data: Labs: Plt 88 (L), AST 142 (H), ALT 128 (H), Creatinine 1.2 (H), LDH 680 (H).

Studies: OB ultrasound: fetus cephalic, normal fluid, EFW 3200g.

Assessment: 34-year-old at 38 weeks with severe features of preeclampsia, concerning for HELLP syndrome.

Plan:
1. Preeclampsia with severe features / possible HELLP
- Magnesium sulfate seizure prophylaxis
- Betamethasone not indicated at term; plan delivery
- OB consult, continuous maternal/fetal monitoring
2. Thrombocytopenia and elevated LFTs
- Repeat CBC and LFTs q6h
- Type and screen, anesthesia consult
